newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Howard says decision on Australia media laws soon.
newsitem.headline: Howard says decision on Australia media laws soon.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday that a decision would be taken soon on media laws, and added most people with an opinion were talking from a position of self interest.
"We'll take a decision soon, we've had other things on our plate this week," Howard said when asked when a decision on possible changes to media ownership laws would occur.

Howard said while he was aware of the views of the Packer family on the removal of cross media ownership restrictions, the decision would be taken by the Parliament and nobody else would decide whether the law would change.
"Everybody's got a point a view on this, and can I tell you, most people talk from self interest," Howard told Melbourne Radio 3AW.
Australia's Liberal-National government has conducted a private inquiry into laws restricting cross ownership of television stations and newspapers and has indicated it may ease existing limits.
Existing laws prevent a television operator owning more than 15 percent of a major newspaper in the same market and vice versa.

There has been widespread speculation that Kerry Packer, whose Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd owns the Nine television network and several magazine titles, will make a takeover bid for newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd if the media laws are changed.
Packer owns 15 percent of Fairfax, the maximum allowed under current cross-media rules.
